main_body: Flat-roofed desert building: a large sand-coloured roof deck with a teal dome, over a brick front wall with an arched door and a small barred window
top_band: Sand/tan roof deck, rows ~3-33, with a darker inner parapet edge on the left and top and a lighter front lip at rows ~31-33
evidence: Down the middle column, the speckled sand roof surface fills rows 3-30 with a parapet rim. A lighter front-edge lip at rows 31-33 follows, then a dark brown eave shadow at rows 34-35. Below that is the brick wall (rows 36-65) with a door and window. The roof reads clearly as a horizontal surface seen from above, and the front face is a separate vertical plane. The door has a pale frame and the window has a sill and dark lattice, so both read as inset. The flat roof is very tall for a foreshortened top, but it is clearly drawn as a roof deck with a parapet and a dome that has a visible base.

style.evidence: The dome has about 5-6 teal steps with per-block highlights. The sand roof has 4-5 tones plus speckle. The bricks use light, mid and dark tones with dark brown mortar, and the outlines are tinted brown rather than black. The door has plank shading and gold studs. The surfaces carry real speckle and grain, with no large flat fills. Overall it is slightly less dense than the tiled references, but a careful artist would accept it beside them.
